CONTROLS.DESCRIPTION: The colour the rig is showing. Driven over OSC by eclipse-dmx, same as the other Link scenes. It only shows through when no media is loaded - it tints the fallback test pattern so the CRT has something to chew on before you have baked your text into the media. Declared FIRST so it keeps the positional address /controls/global/color/1, and named rig_color so /controls/scene/rigcolor also finds it - see scenes/readme.md.
CONTROLS.NAME: rig_color

CONTROLS.DESCRIPTION: The CRT itself. On, the source is run through the RVM filter (Lottes' Retro Video Monitor, arcade slot-mask mode). Off, the source is passed straight through, upscaled clean - which is the 'clean' preset and the way to see what the filter is actually doing by toggling it.
CONTROLS.NAME: crt_enable

CONTROLS.DESCRIPTION: Screen curvature. 0 is a flat panel; 1 is the barrel warp RVM ships as its arcade default. Above 1 bulges further and starts to vignette the corners away. This is a runtime knob because RVM takes the warp amount as a function argument - only the mask *style* (arcade vs TV vs PVM) is compile-time, and this scene commits to arcade.
CONTROLS.NAME: warp

CONTROLS.DESCRIPTION: Horizontal spot size. 0.50 is a soft, blurry beam; 0.75 is RVM's default; 1.00 is a hard, blocky pixel. This is the INPUT_BLUR the filter takes as an argument, so it moves live.
CONTROLS.NAME: blur

CONTROLS.DESCRIPTION: Output level, applied after the filter. A slot mask throws away roughly two thirds of the light on purpose (that is how it makes the black grid between phosphors), so a CRT run wants headroom above 1 to get back to the brightness of the clean pass. Leave at 1 while dialling the look in.
CONTROLS.NAME: brightness

CREDIT: eclipse-os; RVM filter by Timothy Lottes (public domain)
DESCRIPTION: A CRT styliser: your media (with the text baked into it) run through Timothy Lottes' Retro Video Monitor filter in arcade slot-mask mode. Pass 0 draws the source into a low-res buffer; the final pass upscales it with scanlines, a slot mask and barrel warp. Warp, spot size and brightness are live; the mask style is committed to arcade.

PASSES.DESCRIPTION: The source, at the CRT's native resolution. 640x360 is the 'input' the filter upscales - low enough that 360 scanlines land visibly across a 1080 output (~3x), 16:9 so media is not stretched. Raise it for a finer tube, lower it for a chunkier one. FLOAT so the linear-light maths in the filter has the precision for it.

TITLE: Eclipse CRT
